title: pkix-revocation-http errors do not derive Clone/Eq
description:
pkix-revocation-http defines two public error types:
- `ExtractError` — derives only `Debug`, missing `Clone, PartialEq, Eq, #[non_exhaustive]` is present but no serde.
- `FetchError` — derives only `Debug`, missing `Clone, PartialEq, Eq`. Documented as intentional because `FetchError::Transport(Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>)` is not Clone/Eq.

AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6: 'Public result/error types ... MUST derive Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq and MUST be Send + Sync.'

`ExtractError` wraps `der::Error`, which does implement Clone + PartialEq. There is no structural reason ExtractError cannot derive Clone + PartialEq + Eq. The missing derives are an oversight, not a necessary exception.

`FetchError` has a legitimate exception for the Transport variant's `Box<dyn Error>`, which is documented. But FetchError also lacks a Send+Sync compile-time assertion. Since `Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>` IS Send+Sync, the whole enum is auto-Send+Sync but no compile-time assertion pins it.

Impact: callers cannot cache `ExtractError` values or compare them in tests without converting to String first. This makes ExtractError a second-class citizen compared to every other workspace error.

Locations: /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-revocation-http/src/lib.rs lines 158-164 (ExtractError), lines 290-299 (FetchError)
